newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge on weak data, broker woes.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs surge on weak data, broker woes.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures shot to new contract highs on Wednesday as Japan's weak industrial output data and widening brokerage scandals reinforced hopes of rates remaining steady.

Dealers said news of a raid at the offices of Yamaichi Securities and of the brokerage's involvement with racketeers underpinned the market as it indicated Japan's financial sector woes were far from over.
Japan's industrial output fell 3.1 percent month-on-month in June, against an average forecast of a 2.8 percent fall.
Dealers said the Japanese interest rate market had opened on a bullish note on rumours of a four percent fall in June industrial production.

The announcement by the Japanese Ministry of Finance of a raft of punitive measures against Nomura Securities and Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank for their involvement in a racketeer payoff scandal also contributed to the market's firm tone, dealers said.
The lead March Euroyen contract breached resistance at 99.13 and 99.15, rising to a high of 99.18 as September JGBs climbed to 126.35.
March Euroyen stood at 99.18 at 1110 GMT against its IMM close at 99.11 on active volume of 25,080 lots.
September JGBs settled at 126.38 against a previous 125.76.
A dealer at a European futures house said stop-loss buy orders were triggered above 126.00 and the contract faced immediate resistance around 126.50.

Eurodollar futures ended higher in line with strength in U.S. treasuries, which were boosted by a relatively tame second quarter employment cost index and news of a balanced budget pact between Democrats and Republicans.
December Eurodollars ended at 94.165 against an IMM close at 94.155 on volume of 3,290 lots.
